CSC 115.name: Python Programming for Everyone
CSC 115.description: Introduces Python programming through variables, control flow, methods, collections and object-oriented design.
CSC 115.rationale: The source centers on general programming constructs and implementation.
CSC 115.prerequisites: Pre/Corequisite: MTH 107 , or Math SAT score of 620, or ACT score of 27, or ALEKS score of 61.
CSC 115.locator: CSC 115 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 210.name: Computing for Scientists
CSC 210.description: Combines algorithm implementation and computing tools with scientific data storage, analysis and visualization.
CSC 210.rationale: Programming methods and scientific computing applications share the brief description; neither is sufficiently dominant for a single narrower category.
CSC 210.prerequisites: Prerequisite: MTH 141 or MTH 151 or MTH 161 or MTH 171 .
CSC 210.locator: CSC 210 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 322.name: System Programming
CSC 322.description: Develops UNIX system programming using C, shell tools, system calls, processes, threads, files, signals and network interfaces.
CSC 322.rationale: C programming supports the primary focus on operating-system interfaces and system resources.
CSC 322.prerequisites: Prerequisite: CSC 220 or ECE 218 , and CSC 314 .
CSC 322.locator: CSC 322 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 329.name: Introduction to Game Programming
CSC 329.description: Uses a team-built game to teach software design, version control, graphics, interfaces and networked implementation.
CSC 329.rationale: Game development supplies the project context for software construction rather than independent game-domain or AI instruction.
CSC 329.locator: CSC 329 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 405.name: Computer Science Seminars Reports
CSC 405.description: Students attend departmental computer-science seminars and write reports on their varying subjects.
CSC 405.rationale: The seminar subjects are unspecified; report writing alone does not establish a primary communication or technical category.
CSC 405.prerequisites: Prerequisite: At least 12 credits of CSC courses.
CSC 405.locator: CSC 405 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 410.name: Computer Science Project Planning
CSC 410.description: Plans a computing project through requirements analysis, architecture, algorithm selection, interface design, validation and prototyping. The source permits1–3 credit hours.
CSC 410.rationale: The stated content consists of general software design and development methods; program-specific approval of a DS/AI topic does not turn those methods into AI course content.
CSC 410.prerequisites: Prerequisite: At least 12 credits of CSC courses.
CSC 410.locator: CSC 410 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 411.name: Computer Science Project Implementation
CSC 411.description: Implements and integrates a computing project, covering components, verification, validation and documentation. The source permits1–3 credit hours.
CSC 411.rationale: Implementation, integration and testing establish general software construction; unspecified hardware preparation does not establish systems as the dominant subject.
CSC 411.prerequisites: Prerequisite: At least 12 credits of CSC courses.
CSC 411.locator: CSC 411 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 412.name: Computer Science Internship
CSC 412.description: Places students in commercial computing work, normally requiring50 documented internship hours per earned credit. The source permits1–3 credit hours.
CSC 412.rationale: The host work and substantive topic are unspecified. Degree approval does not provide a course-level AI or programming content description.
CSC 412.prerequisites: Prerequisite: At least 12 credits of CSC courses.
CSC 412.locator: CSC 412 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 423.name: Database Systems
CSC 423.description: Covers information models, relational database design, query languages and database-backed web programming, with introductory mining concepts.
CSC 423.rationale: Database organization, design and access dominate the description.
CSC 423.locator: CSC 423 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 431.name: Introduction to Software Engineering
CSC 431.description: Studies software processes from requirements and design through validation and evolution, including project tools, interaction and professional risks.
CSC 431.rationale: Software engineering methods are the primary subject; legal and interaction considerations support that development focus.
CSC 431.prerequisites: Prerequisite: CSC 317 or CSC 322 or CSC 517.
CSC 431.locator: CSC 431 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 506.name: Logic and Automated Reasoning
CSC 506.description: Combines formal logic and incompleteness with resolution, proof-search methods and automated theorem-proving systems.
CSC 506.rationale: The description gives substantial attention both to mathematical logic and to automated-reasoning methods; neither component is reduced to an incidental application.
CSC 506.prerequisites: Prerequisite: CSC317 or CSC545 and MTH309 or MTH230.
CSC 506.locator: CSC 506 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 542.name: Statistical Learning with Applications
CSC 542.description: Applies supervised and unsupervised statistical learning in R, including regression, classification, clustering and dimensionality reduction.
CSC 542.rationale: Explicit statistical machine-learning models and their application establish AI/ML rather than general statistics alone.
CSC 542.locator: CSC 542 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 543.name: Computer Vision with Deep Learning
CSC 543.description: Uses deep-learning projects in PyTorch to analyze, process and generate images.
CSC 543.rationale: Deep neural methods for computer vision and image generation are explicitly central.
CSC 543.locator: CSC 543 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 548.name: Problem Solving for Bioinformatics
CSC 548.description: Combines Perl programming with genome and protein inference, biological-network analysis and machine-learning applications to biomedical data.
CSC 548.rationale: The source explicitly combines substantial programming instruction, learning methods and biological prediction; a single dominant subject is not established.
CSC 548.locator: CSC 548 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 549.name: Biomedical Data Science
CSC 549.description: Develops scripting and computational workflows for genomic data, including sequencing analysis, version control and responsible research.
CSC 549.rationale: Programming skills and substantive genomic-data analysis are interwoven; the description does not establish either as incidental.
CSC 549.locator: CSC 549 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field

CSC 550.name: Computational Neuroscience
CSC 550.description: Models neural systems from individual neurons to perception and behavior, with MATLAB practice and links to machine learning.
CSC 550.rationale: Neuroscience is the primary domain; connections to machine learning do not establish an AI-methods course.
CSC 550.locator: CSC 550 entire course block, including credit amount/range and eligibility field
